text:
sana_infra: kicking off kubeadm bootstrap for ap-southeast2 spot-backed GPU nodepool (3 nodes). plan: kubeadm single-controlplane, worker nodepool named nodepool-gpu-spot, taint gpu=true:NoSchedule, use mixed spot instances with fallback to ondemand. posting preflight and cost tradeoffs.

matt_ops: nice — are we using the new spot-termination-handler image and drain hooks? last time we had pods stuck during reclaim.

sana_infra: yes, using `spot-termination-handler:v2.1.0` as a DaemonSet. also enabling `node-critical-startup` probe to skip heavy init on reclaim events.

jules_oncall: ETA for bootstrap? i can be on standby for network smoke.

sana_infra: starting now. first step: `kubeadm init --config /etc/kubeadm/apse2-bootstrap.yaml` then apply CNI (calico), metrics-server, and gpu-operator. will paste logs/errors if any.

deploy-bot: InstanceGroup create requested: ig-nodepool-gpu-spot-3 (type p4d/xlarge-ish, spot, maxPrice 0.25, fallbackPolicy: ondemand).

sana_infra: init output: "[kubeadm] Using manifest folder \"/etc/kubernetes/manifests\"" then error: `unable to validate iptables: connection refused` — looks like host firewall was still active on control-plane node.

matt_ops: did we run the preflight script that toggles br_netfilter and iptables? called `infra/scripts/preflight-bridge.sh` on the image?

sana_infra: i did, but docker overlay had stale nft rules. fixed by `iptables -t nat -F ; iptables -t nat -X` then re-run init.

rami_platform: note re: cost tradeoffs — spot interruption rate for this AZ historically ~3% daily. if we want <1% risk, either use a mixed-az pool or reserve one ondemand replica.

jules_oncall: for validation checklist: 1) kube-system pods healthy 2) calico BGP adjacency 3) metrics-server responsive 4) GPU driver bound 5) node taints and labels correct 6) kubelet eviction thresholds sane

sana_infra: post-init logs: all control-plane apis up. applied CNI: calico v3.26.0. calico nodes reported 3/3 ready.

sana_infra: next applied gpu-operator helm chart (nv/gpu-operator v1.11). driver pod went CrashLoopBackOff on node-2 with: `nvidia-smi not found`.

matt_ops: that usually means AMI missing NVIDIA driver or the install hook couldn't access kernel headers. what image are these nodes using?

sana_infra: using our golden-ubuntu-22.04-gpu-2026-03 image — it should have dkms/nvidia preinstalled. i see in cloud-init logs `dkms: failed to build module nvidia` due to mismatched kernel `5.19.0-custom` vs installed headers 5.19.0-aws.

rami_platform: rollback plan: either rebuild image with correct headers or set node taint so we can spin one temporary ondemand node with proper image for driver install. cost wise, a single ondemand warmup node is cheap but avoids service impact.

jules_oncall: agree, do 1 ondemand warm node, run GPU-driver bootstrap, then roll spot nodes as cordoned. leave taint so pods don't schedule until GPU available.

sana_infra: spinning ondemand node now (`ig-nodepool-gpu-ondemand-1`). deploy-bot: instance provision started.

deploy-bot: instance ig-nodepool-gpu-ondemand-1 id i-0abcd1234 provisioned.

sana_infra: ran `kubectl label node i-0abcd1234 gpu=preflight` and `kubectl taint node i-0abcd1234 gpu=preflight:NoSchedule-` to allow driver install. installed matching headers and rebooted. driver install now passes `nvidia-smi`.

matt_ops: once driver is present, drain and cordon the node, then create a kubeadm node join token and re-register the node to the spot pool? also ensure the cloud-init attaches the right kernel-headers package.

sana_infra: joined node back as `node-gpu-01`. gpu-operator now sees device plugin, `nvidia.com/gpu` capacity 8.

rami_platform: cost note for handoff doc: recommended default for spot-GPU pools = 1 warm ondemand replica per 3 spot nodes OR multi-az spread. record in provisioning runbook with commands used and AMI / kernel header check.

jules_oncall: smoke tests: run `kubectl run cuda-smoke --image=nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime --restart=Never --limits='nvidia.com/gpu=1' -- sleep 30` and check pod exit code 0.

sana_infra: smoke ran, pod passed, latency to pull image ~45s. metrics-server shows node metrics. calico BGP adjacency stable.

matt_ops: network quirks: remember to add iptables NAT preflight in cluster-autoscaler-config so drain hooks don't hit SNAT issues. Add `--skip-nat-check=false`? also ensure kube-proxy is in iptables mode not ipvs (we prefer iptables for older kernels).

sana_infra: noted. updating runbook snippet: ```
# preflight checklist
sysctl -w net.bridge.bridge-nf-call-iptables=1
apt-get install -y linux-headers-$(uname -r)
ensure dkms/nvidia packages match kernel
apply taint: kubectl taint nodes <name> gpu=true:NoSchedule
```

rami_platform: for handoff, include cost calc example: 3 x spot p4 equiv (~$3.2/hr each historically) + 1 ondemand warm ($4.5/hr) => expect baseline ~$13/hr; with interruptions ~+20% transient overhead for restarts. note these are region-specific.

jules_oncall: ok i'm satisfied to sign off on handoff once you: 1) add AMI/kernel header check to image build job 2) add warm-ondemand recommendation to runbook 3) document drain hooks used and daemonset versions 4) capture `kubectl get nodes -o wide` output in the doc

sana_infra: will update runbook and push to `docs/provisioning/ap-se2-gpu-spot.md`. handing off to oncall rotation for next 72h monitoring. thanks all :thumbsup:

matt_ops: thx — if we see >5% interruption rate we'll either increase warm replica or change AZ mix.

jules_oncall: i'll put a 72h alert window in oncall playbook and watch pod restarts for GPU nodes.

deploy-bot: action: label applied to node-gpu-01 (gpu=ready), annotation `handed-off-by=sana_infra` added.

sana_infra: leaving note: follow-up item to add kernel header verification step into our image CI (ticket INFRA-1298).

jules_oncall: acknowledged. closing thread after runbook commits and postmortem if anything spikes.
